name: Water In and For the Economy
description:
India is home to 18% of the global population, but has only 4% of the world’s available freshwater resources. In an increasingly warming world, water may yet become India’s weakest link. This panel discussion explores water as both a critical challenge and a strategic resource for India’s economic future. Based on the book Water, Nature, Progress: Solutions for a New India, the discussion presents a blueprint for action through policy reform, public finance, private investment and behavioural change. 
As the ultimate resource, the impact of water on public health, energy, agriculture, urbanization, infrastructure, manufacturing and human development is pervasive, making water resource management vital to the country’s future. The issues at hand are complicated, from the need for equity between the agricultural, industrial and commercial sectors and the impact of unsustainable water management to increased urbanization and climate change. Governed differently, though, water could become a key driver of sustainable economic transformation.

name: It’s Time to Put Nutrition First
description:
Sylvia Karpagam discusses her book Meat of the Matter, challenging prejudices and misconceptions around food in India. Is malnutrition in India simply a policy failure, or are there structural conditions which make it so? 
The conversation explores the political, social, and economic contexts surrounding food practices across the country, arguing that malnutrition is structural, not incidental. Beyond failing policies and poorly implemented programmes, Karpagam highlights the role discrimination plays at every level, implicating researchers, academicians, bureaucrats, elected representatives, and the media in perpetuating stereotypical narratives that need to be broken. Small improvements in nutritional indicators, she argues, cannot be read as “successes,” since those left behind face outcomes that are significant, and often irreversible.

name: Non-Aligned Modernism
description:
What does it mean to build a nation’s identity from scratch? This lecture traces the life of Aditya Prakash, one of India’s first Modernist architects. His son, Vikramaditya Prakash, explores his body of work that reflects the idea of non-aligned modernism — a third way of building a modern, internationalist identity of a newly independent nation, resisting allegiance to either capitalist or communist blocs. 
Born in 1924 in colonial India, Aditya Prakash trained in London before joining the Chandigarh Capital office as a junior architect under Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret. Over the following decades, he designed nearly 100 buildings and urban plans, while also working as an artist, sculptor, furniture designer, and theatre actor. For him, architecture, sculpture, and performance were never separate disciplines, but expressions of a single question: how to live fully while keeping the interests of the poorest at heart. He called this his “continuous line” — the philosophical thread that ran through everything he made.

name: Antarnaad
description:
The call of the soul can be heard this evening. 
Rakshit Kulkarni’s recital features two Hindustani rāgas, presented in their traditional depth and grandeur. This is followed by a selection of rare Haridasa compositions in the second half of the concert. He is accompanied by Mihir Kalyanpur on tabla and Anjana Hegde on harmonium. 
The Haridasa tradition began in Karnataka centuries ago, blossoming from the Dvaita philosophy of Madhvacharya. Saint-composers like Purandara Dasa and Kanaka Dasa wrote devotional songs in Kannada, making sacred philosophy accessible to ordinary people. These compositions were originally sung in the Carnatic style, but over time, particularly in North Karnataka, Hindustani music began to shape how Haridasa songs were rendered. Vocalists like Bhimsen Joshi carried this crossover forward, and it continues today. This recital brings together both traditions, presenting Haridasa compositions through a Hindustani lens.

name: Re-Garde
description:
Re-Garde is a contemporary dance piece moving between opposing pairs: youth and old age, control and release. As the choreographers describe it, the piece traces how our way of observing the world, people, art, conflict, each other, transforms from childhood to adulthood, shaped by the societies and environments we inhabit. 
Exploring the sense of sight, the performance follows two performers as mirrors of each other’s projections, ready to give, lose, provoke and be provoked; crossing the delicate boundaries that separate them, suspended between gesture and poetry. What does it mean to look at the world clear-sighted, unconditioned, free?  
MF Company:
MF Company is a contemporary dance and physical theatre company founded by Maxime Freixas and Francesco Colaleo. Since 2014, they’ve performed internationally across festivals in France, Italy, Poland, Spain, Germany and beyond, exploring humorous, physical and committed research of the body, rhythm and dynamic space. They have been supported by DRAC ARA, the French Institute (FR, MA, PL, IT, HU), the Metropolis and the City of Lyon. 
BIC Elsewhere:
While the majority of our events find a home at our premises in Domlur, BIC Elsewhere represents our commitment to bringing conversations, arts, and culture directly to diverse audiences. Through this initiative, we collaborate with various venues, extending the reach of our events beyond our own space. These partnerships not only breathe life into our gatherings but also play a crucial role in cultivating an environment for the flourishing of arts and culture in the city.

name: Kuchipudi Yakshaganam
description:
At 85 years of age, Guru Sri Pasumarthi Rattaiah Sarma Garu remains one of the last living custodians of the Kuchipudi Yakshagana tradition, a dance-drama format that seamlessly integrates dance, music, abhinaya, dialogue, and the singing of padyams by the performer. Kuchipudi dancer Aishwarya Meenakshi presents this evening, offering a chance to witness dharavus from this near-forgotten repertoire. 
Distinct from the solo recital format commonly seen today, Kuchipudi Yakshaganam is a collaborative and immersive performance practice accompanied by a live orchestra, preserving the form’s historic character as a total theatre tradition. This presentation serves as an act of cultural preservation and transmission. It is a rare opportunity to encounter, celebrate, and document a vital chapter in the history of Kuchipudi directly from one of its most distinguished torchbearers.

name: Playful Body
description:
Centred on partnering, play, and humour, in this workshop participants will explore how to observe, listen and respond to the bodies all around.  
The class opens with floor work rooted in the cranio-sacral connection and the body’s spiral, moving instinctively and fluidly. Participants explore coordination and movement quality before the work evolves into partnering: exploring gravity, counterweight, off-axis balance and sensory listening through touch. It is a practice built on trust, joy and calculated risk; balancing between falling and rising, letting gravity move through the body. 
The session is led by Maxime Freixas and Francesco Colaleo, both pedagogues trained at the National Dance Centre of Lyon. They have taught across France, Italy, Poland, China and beyond, and created Falling Superstars for CODARTS’ Dance Teacher Bachelor programme in 2024.  
Please Note: The workshop is intended for Intermediate level practitioners. Though open to all ages, participants are expected to be in good physical health with no particular physical fragilities. The session has a limited capacity of 20 participants.

name: Dear Kannamma
description:
Languages: English, Tamil, and Sanskrit 
 
Inspired by the life and works of Mahakavi Subramanya Bharathi, imagined and told through the voice of his muse, his kannamma, this solo bharatnatyam dance-theatre is an ode to the man and his poetry that continues to influence and inspire current generations. The performance is accompanied by live music. 
Bharathi’s journey, from journalist and household rebel to revolutionary and Vedantin, is a colourful one. His private devotion to Chellammal and his public awakening to the Mother, Kali, Sister Nivedita and Bharat Mata, become inseparable. From Benaras to Bengal to Pondicherry to Kadayam, Dear Kannamma seeks the person and the poet, the muse and the goddess, the beloved and the motherland.

name: Let's Get Bangalored!
description:
Bengaluru’s rapid expansion means paving over decades of history, one flyover and glass tower at a time. Arun Pai brings his 2007 BIC talk on the city’s history and heritage into the present, asking what’s been lost, and what still remains, beneath the city’s relentless growth. 
Pai has been walking Bengaluru’s streets since 2005 as Founder of BangaloreWALKS, telling the city’s story to everyone from first-time visitors to Prime Ministers, global CEOs, and G20 delegations, as Bengaluru has grown into one of the world’s fastest-growing cities. He brings these encounters into conversation with a provocation: that Bengaluru’s real strength lies not in preserving its built heritage, but in its ability to constantly reinvent itself. Expect stories from his years as the self-appointed “Footpath Mayor” of Bengaluru, and Brand Ambassador for Swachha Bengaluru too, as he makes the case for a city that looks forward as often as it looks back. 
This talk is part of a series marking twenty years of BIC, in which speakers from the institution’s early years return to revisit topics they first addressed here. It is a chance to trace what has changed, what has endured, and how ideas evolve over time. BIC is proud to have been host to conversations that connect culture, ideas, and public life across two decades.

name: Melodies and Memories
description:
A tribute to a voice that deserves to be heard across generations, Melodies & Memories celebrates the extraordinary life and musical legacy of legendary playback singer Suman Kalyanpur. This session is an immersive journey through the songs, stories and memories that defined one of Indian cinema’s most graceful and enduring voices. 
Interwoven with live performances are engaging anecdotes, little-known facts and fascinating insights into the people, collaborations and moments that shaped her career. Thoughtfully curated by Sandhya S Kumar, the programme blends scholarship with nostalgia, offering audiences an opportunity to rediscover Suman Kalyanpur’s timeless contribution to Indian film music.

name: Echoes of Strings
description:
Swaradhya is a Bangalore-based World Fusion Instrumental Band blending Indian classical music with contemporary western genres. Led by sitarist Ashok Ayengar, the band includes Natraj Nirvikar (piano, keys, guitar), Kapil Dalal (double bass), and Ashish Padiyar (percussion). Their repertoire spans original raga-based compositions fused with global rhythms (latin, afro, etc.), alongside fresh adaptations of Indian thumris and folk music. 
This concert blends Indian Classical influences with contemporary acoustic expression to create a truly unique soundscape. Exploring emotion, memory, and nature through the voice strings, the session invites audiences into inner reflection. The concert moves from meditative stillness to rhythmic exploration in a medley of cultural influences, creating space for every listener to weave their own emotions, memories and stories into the music.
